name: Product Hunt
price_note: Posting a product is free. You need a personal account, and new accounts have to be given access to post first.
audience: Early adopters, makers, investors and tech press, mostly English-speaking.
how_it_works: You post your own product from a personal account; company accounts cannot post, and you do not need a hunter. Products go live on a daily leaderboard where members upvote and comment. A draft can be saved until you are ready to schedule the launch day.
tips: Request posting access well before launch day if your account is new.
Post it yourself rather than through a hunter, so you control the page.
Be in the comments all day: answer every question in your own words.
Point launch traffic at a page that explains the product without a signup wall.

name: Hacker News (Show HN)
price_note: Free. There is no paid placement.
audience: Programmers, founders and technical readers who will try the thing and say exactly what they think.
how_it_works: Submit a normal story whose title starts with "Show HN". It has to be something people can try now, that you made yourself and are around to discuss; landing pages, sign-up pages and fundraisers are off topic. Every Show HN appears on the newest list, and enough points move it onto the Show page.
tips: Let people try it without a sign-up or email if you possibly can.
Start the thread with a comment on how and why you built it.
Never ask friends to upvote or comment; the guidelines forbid it.
Minor version bumps are not a Show HN; a major overhaul can be.

name: Uneed
price_note: Free launches wait in a queue. Fast-track ($19.99) gets you a slot in about 14 days; Skip the line ($39.99) lets you pick your launch date.
audience: Indie makers, founders and people looking for new tools.
how_it_works: Paste your URL and Uneed reads your page to pre-fill the listing; you sign up only to save it. Free products join a waiting line for a launch day, or you pay to pick the date. On launch day products compete on a daily ladder.
tips: Count the free waiting line into your plan; it can be weeks.
If your site blocks crawlers, be ready to fill the details in by hand.
Keep the listing current after launch: Uneed keeps sending traffic over time.

name: Microlaunch
price_note: Paid packs on the page we read: Launch Pro $49 (often discounted to $39), Launch Plus $99, Launch Everywhere $199 with 50+ directory submissions, and a $299 product review. We did not see a free launch option confirmed today.
audience: Makers and early adopters who rate products and leave written roasts.
how_it_works: Products launch for a whole month instead of a single day, on a monthly leaderboard. Visitors score the idea and the product and leave written feedback called roasts. Re-launching is allowed for major feature releases.
tips: Plan for a month of activity, not a single launch day.
Ask for roasts: the written feedback is the most useful part.
Offer a deal on the listing; there is a deals section that gets its own traffic.

name: Peerlist Launchpad
audience: Developers, designers and other builders with Peerlist profiles.
how_it_works: Launchpad is a weekly launch board inside Peerlist, the professional network for builders. Projects are voted on during the week and voting closes on a countdown. Peerlist says it accepts a limited number of projects each week.
tips: Fill in your Peerlist profile first; voters look at who made it.
Launch early in the week so you get the whole voting window.
Weekly slots are limited, so do not leave it to the last day.

name: BetaList
price_note: Every submission is paid (Lite, Standard or Premium plans); prices appear only when you pick a plan. Declined submissions are refunded.
audience: Early adopters who sign up for new startups, pre-launch or live; about 20 are featured a day, plus a newsletter.
how_it_works: You (or your coding agent, through a public API) draft a submission, then claim it, pick a plan and pay. A person reviews and edits every listing before it is scheduled. A website featured in the last 12 months is refused as a duplicate.
tips: Use your own domain; app-store, Notion and free-subdomain links are refused.
Keep the pitch to one plain sentence under 75 characters, without the product name.
Have a square icon and at least one screenshot ready; you cannot pay without them.
BetaList publishes agent instructions at betalist.com/agent if you want your agent to draft it.

name: Launching Next
price_note: Free to submit. A $99 upgrade gets your startup considered within one business day.
audience: Founders and readers following new startups, plus a weekly email.
how_it_works: You fill in a form about your startup and the team reviews submissions every day. You get an email if it is published. Free submissions wait in the normal queue; the paid upgrade only speeds up the review.
tips: Submit well ahead of your launch date if you use the free queue.
Write the description for a reader who has never heard of you.

name: Indie Hackers
audience: Bootstrapped founders sharing revenue, growth and lessons in public.
how_it_works: Indie Hackers has a products directory where makers list what they build and post updates under it. Adding a product needs an account. Most attention comes from posts in the community, not the listing itself.
tips: Write a post about what you learned building it, not an announcement.
Post milestone updates on the product page over time.

name: DevHunt
price_note: Listing is free. Advertising is sold separately.
audience: Developers voting on new developer tools.
how_it_works: Makers launch developer tools in weekly batches and developers upvote them; each week has a winner. Products that are not for developers are shown but left out of the vote. You sign in to submit.
tips: Only launch here if developers are your users; others are left out of the vote.
Launch at the start of a week to get the full voting window.
Show code, an API call or a CLI in your screenshots.

name: Fazier
price_note: Fazier says you can submit for free. We did not confirm its paid options.
audience: People browsing new tech products every day.
how_it_works: Fazier lists a new batch of launches every day, each tagged with its pricing model. You sign in to submit. Launches are grouped by day on the front page.
tips: Mark your pricing model honestly; it is shown next to the name.
A short, concrete tagline matters: the front page shows little else.

name: TinyLaunch
price_note: Standard launch is free. Premium launch is $39 per launch (skips the queue, guaranteed backlink). Featured spots are sold separately.
audience: Indie makers and small-startup founders.
how_it_works: Products launch on the homepage and stay up for several days in a ranking. The top three get a badge and a backlink. Free launches wait in a standard queue; paid launches skip it.
tips: The backlink for top-3 products requires embedding their badge with a link back.
If you launch free, schedule it around the queue, not your release.

name: SaaSHub
price_note: Submitting and SaaSHub Launch are free for makers.
audience: People comparing software and looking for alternatives to a tool they use.
how_it_works: You submit a product with its categories and competitors, and it is listed as an alternative to those competitors. Submissions without listed competitors go to the bottom of the queue. SaaSHub Launch is a separate daily lineup of 12 products that need at least three confirmed supporters each.
tips: List your real competitors; it decides where you appear.
Verify the product with an email on its own domain for a faster review.
For SaaSHub Launch, collect supporters outside your own company; teammates do not count.

name: AlternativeTo
audience: People searching for a replacement for software they already use.
how_it_works: AlternativeTo is a crowd-sourced list of software alternatives. Users add apps and say which existing apps they replace, and others vote. Being listed next to a well-known app is what brings visitors.
tips: Add your product as an alternative to the specific tools people want to leave.
Ask happy users to like it; ranking on each comparison page depends on it.

name: r/SideProject
price_note: Free; posting needs a Reddit account.
audience: Makers sharing and commenting on each other's side projects.
how_it_works: A Reddit community where people post what they built and ask for feedback. Posts rise by votes and comments. Read the subreddit rules in the sidebar before posting; they change.
tips: Post as a person asking for feedback, not as an advert.
A short demo video or GIF does far better than a link alone.
Reply to every comment in the first few hours.

name: There's An AI For That
price_note: One-time fee: $49 basic listing or $437 with a newsletter placement. One tool a month is listed free from a thread they run on X. Refunded if not published.
audience: People searching for an AI tool for a specific task.
how_it_works: You pay a one-time review fee and staff review every submission, usually in one to two days. Listings do not expire. MCP servers are accepted.
tips: Only submit AI products; it is an AI-only directory.
Make the task your tool does obvious in the name and first line; people search by task.
Have your landing page and payments working before it goes live.

name: Toolify
price_note: Submission is $99, with no queue and listing within 48 hours. We did not see a free option on the submit page.
audience: People browsing AI tools, with a large audience outside the US.
how_it_works: Toolify is an AI tools directory with categories and rankings by traffic. Makers pay to submit and can either write the listing themselves in English or let Toolify generate it; Toolify translates listings into other languages.
tips: Write the description yourself if you want control over how the tool is described.
Advertising and featured promotion are sold separately from the listing.

name: SideProjectors
price_note: Basic submissions and browsing are free; the site mentions paid extras without listing prices.
audience: Developers who show, sell and buy side projects, or look for a co-founder.
how_it_works: You list a project in one of three ways: to sell it, to find a co-founder, or just to show it. Every project is reviewed before it is approved. Listings for sale include revenue, traffic and tech stack.
tips: Use the showcase listing for launch; the sale listing is for handing the project on.
Include a working demo and screenshots; the review favours complete listings.

name: OpenAlternative
audience: People looking for open-source replacements for paid software.
how_it_works: OpenAlternative lists open-source projects next to the proprietary products they replace, with GitHub stars, last commit and licence. Submitting needs a sign-in. It only fits products whose code is open.
tips: Only submit if your code is open source; the listing shows your repository and licence.
Name the paid product you replace; that is how people find you.

name: Twelve Tools
price_note: Free listing if you link back to them, reviewed within 72 hours. Pro is $36 one-time: no backlink needed, listed within 24 hours.
audience: People browsing a short daily pick of new tools.
how_it_works: Twelve new tools are shown each day. A free listing needs a link back to twelve.tools on your homepage or footer and is reviewed within three days. The paid listing skips the backlink and is featured on the homepage.
tips: Decide whether you want their badge on your site before choosing the free plan.

name: G2
audience: Business buyers comparing software through user reviews.
how_it_works: G2 is a software review site where buyers read verified reviews and category grids. Vendors can create a product profile and invite customers to review it. It pays off once you have customers who will write reviews.
tips: List after you have a handful of customers willing to review.
Pick the category your buyers already browse, not a new one.

name: PitchWall (formerly BetaPage)
price_note: Free launch with at least a 30-day wait. Pro $49 (two-week wait), Premium $99 (your chosen date).
audience: People following new products, now leaning to AI tools, plus a newsletter.
how_it_works: betapage.co now redirects here. You choose a plan: the free launch shows you on the homepage for a day after a wait of 30 days or more; paid plans shorten the wait and add a second day. Every plan includes a backlink.
tips: Submit a month early if you take the free plan.
Old BetaPage links now redirect here; count both domains as one source.

name: Dang.ai
price_note: Free with a backlink to dang.ai and up to 4 weeks' review. Basic $49 (about 4 days). Pro $30 setup then $19 a month.
audience: People browsing AI tools by category.
how_it_works: You create a free account with an email link, then choose a plan. The free plan needs a crawlable link back to dang.ai, allows one category and can take up to four weeks. Paid plans are reviewed faster and get more categories.
tips: Only for AI products.
If you take the free plan, put the backlink up before you submit.

name: EU-Startups Directory
price_note: The submission form offers a free listing that never expires (one image).
audience: European founders, investors and journalists covering European startups.
how_it_works: EU-Startups runs a directory of startups based in Europe alongside its news site. Companies fill in a listing form with their country and sector, and the listing stays up without expiring.
tips: Only fits if your company is based in Europe.

name: e27 Startups
audience: Founders, investors and readers in Southeast Asia and wider Asia.
how_it_works: e27 is an Asian tech media site with a profile directory of startups. Founders create a company profile that readers and investors can browse. The page we opened today showed almost no content, so its current terms are unconfirmed.
tips: Fits best if you sell into Southeast Asia.

name: OpenHunts
price_note: Free launch with 20 slots a week (queue was about 60 weeks; adding their badge skips it). Premium launch $19 (sometimes discounted to $9.90) picks your week. Highlight from $20 to $59 a week.
audience: Makers of small startups and side projects.
how_it_works: Products launch in weekly batches at 8:00 UTC and stay featured on the homepage for seven days. Free launches wait in a long queue unless you add an OpenHunts badge to your site; paid launches choose their week. The top three get a do-follow backlink.
tips: Check the current free-queue length before you plan around it.
Adding their badge is the free way to skip the queue.

name: LaunchIgniter
price_note: Free launch needs their badge and waits for a date. Basic $12 (guaranteed date, backlink), Pro $15 (two extra backlinks), Growth $99 (30 days on the homepage and an editorial review). All one-time.
audience: Makers and early adopters who upvote and review new products.
how_it_works: Products launch on a weekly board where visitors upvote and comment. Every free launch is reviewed by an admin and can be moved if the week fills up. Paid plans get a fixed date and a lasting backlink.
tips: The free plan only gives a backlink to the top three; paid plans include one.
Free launch dates are not guaranteed, so do not tie them to a release.

name: Startup Fame
price_note: Free "Verified" listing if you add their badge to your homepage (about 7 days). Highlight is $19 a month and Spotlight $149 a month for instant, more prominent placement.
audience: Founders looking for exposure and backlinks for a new startup.
how_it_works: Startup Fame is a startup directory with ranked placements. You get listed free by putting its badge on your homepage, which a bot checks, or pay monthly to be listed straight away in a highlighted or spotlight slot.
tips: Keep the badge on your site; the free listing depends on it.
Paid plans are monthly, so cancel if the traffic does not justify it.

name: TopAI.tools
price_note: Fast Track $47 one-time (live within 48 hours, permanent listing). Featured Listing $229 one-time for 7 days featured. Refunded if your tool is not accepted.
audience: People searching for AI tools by task or category.
how_it_works: TopAI.tools is a directory of AI tools. Makers pay once to be reviewed and listed, and new listings appear in a "just landed" section on the homepage. A higher tier adds a week of featured placement and better spots in search and categories.
tips: Every submission is reviewed; tools that are not accepted are refunded automatically.
Listing edits are free afterwards, so keep pricing and screenshots current.

name: Tiny Startups
price_note: Pay what you want: the more you pay, the higher you rank on the board. A free weekly launchpad is still offered at /launch. No minimum price was shown on the pages we read.
audience: Founders and readers looking for small startups that make money.
how_it_works: Tiny Startups is a human-curated launch board and directory, updated daily. Instead of upvotes, placement on the main board follows what each maker chooses to pay, and every spot carries a do-follow backlink. A separate free weekly launchpad remains for makers who do not want to pay.
tips: Use the free weekly launchpad if budget is tight.
Entries are picked by a person, so describe what your product does in plain words.
